'''Mirko pl. Vidaković''' (October 29, 1924 – August 15, 2002<ref name="HAZU"/>) was a [[Croatia]]n [[botany|botanist]] and [[dendrology|dendrologist]] and the expert for the [[genetics]] of the [[forest]] [[tree]]s.

==Biography==

Vidaković was born in [[Lemeš, Bačka|Lemeš]], [[Bačka]].<ref name="HAZU"/> He attained a professional qualification of engineer of forestry before 1949, when he was first employed as a lecturer at the Faculty of Forestry of the [[University of Zagreb]] ({{langx|hr|Šumarski fakultet}}).

He was a full member of [[Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts]] (HAZU) since 1981.<ref name="HAZU"/>

He was the head of the [[Trsteno Arboretum|arboretum in Trsteno]] since 1970.<ref name="HAZU"/>

He worked as [[UNDP]]'s and [[FAO]]'s expert in [[Pakistan]], [[Vietnam]] and [[Hungary]].

Together with forestry of [[Našice]], in 1996 he founded first [[cloning|clone]] seminal [[plantation]] of [[pedunculate oak]] in Croatia.

He died in [[Zagreb]] at the age of 77.

==Works==
His works were published in various editions from international scientific gatherings, symposiums and consultations, mostly in area of ecological valorization of littoral [[carst]], mechanization of [[agriculture]], adaptation of forests to [[climate change]] etc.

He published his works in ''[[Annales forestales]]''.
